_comment: Shared query bank for Google Jobs ingestion. THREE consumers read it, not two: ingest/google-serpapi.py and ingest/google-apify.py (the nightly pipeline) and api/query_claims.py's load_query_buckets() (the contributor claim path, docs/adr/0007). Restructured 2026-07-24 from a flat 24-query list into 4 strategic buckets; the buckets were weighted for one software engineer's job search, and T-37 retargeted THIS RATIONALE -- not the weights and not the query text -- to the Pursuit AI-Native cohort on 2026-08-09: ~30 Builders, entry-level, AI-adjacent, all industries, NYC. Each bucket has its own daily_budget and pick_stale_queries_by_bucket() takes that many least-recently-run queries PER BUCKET, not globally (ingest/google-serpapi.py, and a mirrored implementation in api/query_claims.py) -- so a bucket's share of a scarce day is set here and nowhere else. The budgets sum to 8, which is SerpApi's free tier (250 searches/month) spread over a month; there is NO constant enforcing that sum -- an earlier version of this comment named SERPAPI_DAILY_QUERY_BUDGET, which exists in no module, so the sum is a convention this file holds alone and a bucket edit that breaks it fails silently. Apify's single daily slot (APIFY_DAILY_QUERY_BUDGET=1) draws only from ai_integration + bridge_solutions -- PRIORITY_BUCKETS in ingest/google-apify.py -- since it is the scarcest, most expensive resource and those two buckets are the closest fit to what the cohort is training for. ON THE CONTRIBUTOR PATH, BUCKET ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING AND THE ORDER HERE WAS NOT CHOSEN FOR IT: a claim is capped by MAX_CLAIMS_PER_CONTRIBUTOR_PER_DAY and by the request's own max, and pick_stale_queries_by_bucket() stops at that cap mid-walk, in the order the buckets appear in this file -- so a Builder on a small cap drains core_swe, the least cohort-aligned bucket, before reaching ai_integration. WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT DONE HERE: the daily_budgets, the bucket set and every query string are unchanged. Re-weighting them for the cohort is a real question and it is not answerable yet -- it needs DEV_TASKS.md's OQ-24 (the cohort census) and OQ-26 (the metric that says whether new weights are better). Paid-tier scaling is unchanged: bump each bucket's daily_budget directly (per-bucket comments carry the proposed split) -- no other code change needed.

core_swe._comment: The widest funnel and the loosest fit: generic engineering titles across every industry, which is where the largest number of NYC postings actually live. For the cohort this is the safety net, not the target -- these titles are unqualified by seniority, so most of what comes back is written for people with years of production experience, and nothing in this file filters that out. Entry-level suitability is decided downstream by match.py and score.py, never by the query text; that division is why this bucket can stay broad without swamping a Builder's list. It gets the joint-smallest share of a scarce day for exactly that reason. Paid tier: bump daily_budget to 6.

ai_integration._comment: The bucket the cohort's whole premise points at: prompt, agent, LLM and applied-AI titles are the roles a Builder finishes the program able to argue for on the strength of what they built rather than on years served. Largest daily_budget of the four, and it should stay largest while that premise holds. Two cautions kept from the original weighting because they still apply: these titles are the ones employers are least consistent about naming, so the same job appears here and in bridge_solutions under different words, and the postings skew toward AI-first companies rather than the all-industries spread the cohort is aiming at -- bridge_solutions is what covers the rest. Paid tier: bump daily_budget to 10.

bridge_solutions._comment: Customer-facing AI delivery -- forward deployed, solutions, implementation, technical solutions. These titles hire for AI fluency plus the ability to sit with a customer and explain it, which is a combination a Builder can hold at entry level in a way that 'senior backend engineer' is not, and they are the queries most likely to surface AI work at companies that are not AI companies -- the all-industries half of the cohort's target. This is the bucket where the original weighting and the cohort's needs agree most closely, which is why its rationale changed least. Paid tier: bump daily_budget to 8.

reentry_growth._comment: Written for one person's 2.5-year gap, and it survives the retarget for a different reason than it was created for: a cohort of career changers is entering engineering without a track record to point at, and returnship, return-to-work and re-entry programmes are structured entry points that recruit on training rather than on prior title -- which is the cohort's exact shape. THE QUERY TEXT DOES NOT YET SAY THAT: every query in this bucket still spells 'software engineer', which is the narrower search that was wanted before and is a re-weighting to change, not a comment edit (see the top-level _comment, and OQ-24/OQ-26). Smallest daily_budget of the four because the pool is genuinely narrow -- few employers advertise this framing explicitly at all. Paid tier: bump daily_budget to 4.

queries.query: return to work software engineer remote
